title: Bodhi Day
hookLine: December 8 in Japan: the awakening; Zen monasteries sit for a week

cards: Early December in a Zen monastery in Japan. It's cold. The meditation hall is often unheated.

For the past week, the monks have been sitting from before dawn until late at night, with short breaks for meals, work and a little sleep. On the last night, in many monasteries, nobody lies down at all.
They sit through until morning. Then, just before sunrise, someone looks up at the eastern sky, where one bright point is still shining.

teach.b: Rohatsu means 'the eighth day of the twelfth month.' In Japan, that's when the Buddha's awakening is remembered, and since Japan moved to the solar calendar, temples there keep it on December eighth.

Other East Asian communities mark the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, and in China it's a day for a sweet porridge, laba congee, recalling the milk-rice the Buddha was given before his awakening.
Theravada lands keep the awakening with the birth and the passing, on Vesak. Different calendars, the same night under the tree.
The Pali texts tell the night in three watches. In the first, the Buddha recalled his past lives. In the second, he saw how beings pass away and are reborn according to their deeds.
In the last, he understood suffering, its cause, its end and the way, and his mind was freed.
As the night ended, dawn came.
Later tellings, especially in East Asia, add one detail that has become central in Zen: he looked up, saw the morning star, the planet Venus, low in the eastern sky, and awoke.
Zen retells that moment again and again: a star he had seen many times, seen now completely. The Rohatsu retreat follows the same shape, a week building to a last night without sleep, ending at dawn.
The monks aren't waiting for a star. They're practicing being awake when it rises.

how: In Japanese Zen monasteries, Rohatsu sesshin is a week of intensive sitting in early December, often ending with an all-night sit; many Buddhist communities in the West mark Bodhi Day on December 8 with meditation and readings.

practice: Picture the cold hall, the rows of cushions, the long last night, and feel the stillness of it. Then picture the sky just before dawn, dark blue, one bright point low in the east. Let your attention be as clear as that point.

wordCard.voice: Rohatsu. The eighth day of the twelfth month, when Japanese Buddhists remember the awakening, and Zen monasteries sit through a week that ends at dawn. Today's word.

orig.note: Japanese rohatsu: 'eighth of the twelfth month,' from the old name for the last month of the year.
